description: GALEX imaged the sky in two ultraviolet bands, far-UV (FUV) and near-UV (NUV), fed simultaneously by a dichroic beamsplitter onto two microchannel-plate detectors.
facility_description: The Galaxy Evolution Explorer was a NASA Small Explorer mission led by Caltech, with a 50 cm Ritchey-Chretien telescope; its data are archived at MAST.
notes: MAST's acknowledgement for legacy missions is a template: the page shows the word 'mission' (bold italic) as a placeholder, and lists 'Galaxy Evolution Explorer' among the missions to substitute. The text above is copied verbatim with the placeholder; display it as '...made with the Galaxy Evolution Explorer, obtained from...'. The contract number uses an en dash (NAS5–26555) on the page. MAST data-use page: the quoted sentence has a non-breaking space after 'MAST' in the HTML; it continues 'and therefore do not have restrictions on use', and adds that researchers are expected to acknowledge the mission and STScI. No owner page found that publishes the FUV/NUV effective-area curve files directly (galex.caltech.edu researcher pages now 404); Morrissey et al. (2007) is the calibration paper, but no bands.* reference was added without a quote tying it to the passband tables.
